# Risk Assessment — AI Adoption Project – ABCDE Ltd.

_Generated by Mira · as of 2026-04-24 (week 4, Phase 2: Current State Analysis) · Sources: project_risks.csv, project_description.txt, sample_task_board.csv, project_timeline.csv_

## Summary

The AI Adoption Project at ABCDE Ltd. faces several risks primarily related to data quality and integration challenges. With critical tasks currently blocked or overdue, the likelihood of these risks materializing is heightened, necessitating proactive management to ensure project success.

## Risk register (ranked by likelihood × impact)

| # | ID | Category | Risk | L | I | Score | Most exposed | Live signals | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | R01 | Data Quality & Availability | Incomplete or unstructured data | High | High | 9 | Phase 2: Current State Analysis | T006 Identify data gaps and quality issues (In Progress) | Data scientists |
| 2 | R02 | Integration Issues | Difficulty integrating AI with legacy systems | Medium | High | 6 | Phase 3: Use Case Selection | — | IT professionals |
| 3 | R05 | Ethical & Legal Concerns | Risks of biased models or data privacy violations | Medium | High | 6 | Phase 4: Pilot Design | — | Business stakeholders |
| 4 | R09 | Security Vulnerabilities | AI models targeted by adversarial attacks | Medium | High | 6 | Phase 5: Pilot Implementation | T024 Security review of AI infrastructure (Blocked) | IT professionals |
| 5 | R03 | Talent & Skills Gap | Lack of internal AI/ML expertise | Medium | Medium | 4 | Phase 3: Use Case Selection | — | Business stakeholders |
| 6 | R04 | Change Resistance | Employees resist adopting AI-driven workflows | Medium | Medium | 4 | Phase 4: Pilot Design | — | Cross-functional task force |
| 7 | R06 | Cost Overruns | Underestimation of AI development costs | Medium | Medium | 4 | Phase 5: Pilot Implementation | — | Business stakeholders |
| 8 | R07 | Unrealistic Expectations | Stakeholders expect immediate ROI | Medium | Medium | 4 | Phase 5: Pilot Implementation | — | Cross-functional task force |
| 9 | R08 | Model Performance Drift | AI models lose accuracy over time | Low | Medium | 2 | Phase 6: Evaluation & Iteration | — | Data scientists |
| 10 | R10 | Vendor Lock-in | Overdependence on a specific AI platform | Low | Medium | 2 | Phase 5: Pilot Implementation | — | Business stakeholders |

## Why each risk matters & what to do

**1. R01 Data Quality & Availability** — The overdue task T006 indicates existing data quality issues that could severely impact model performance.  
<sub>Threatens: “reduce manual overhead, minimize errors”</sub>  
Impact (register): Poor model performance and inaccurate outcomes  
Mitigation (register): Perform early data audits and implement robust data governance  
Next step: Conduct a comprehensive data quality audit and address identified gaps before proceeding to the next phase. _(before Phase 3: Use Case Selection)_

**2. R02 Integration Issues** — Integration issues may arise as the project progresses, especially with legacy systems that could disrupt deployment timelines.  
<sub>Threatens: “integrating AI-powered tools into core business functions”</sub>  
Impact (register): Delays in deployment and operational disruptions  
Mitigation (register): Plan integration roadmap and use APIs/middleware  
Next step: Develop a detailed integration roadmap that outlines necessary APIs and middleware solutions. _(before Phase 3: Use Case Selection)_

**3. R05 Ethical & Legal Concerns** — Ethical and legal concerns regarding data usage and model bias could pose significant risks if not addressed early in the project.  
<sub>Threatens: “data-driven decision-making”</sub>  
Impact (register): Legal repercussions and reputational damage  
Mitigation (register): Involve legal early and implement fairness checks  
Next step: Engage legal advisors to review data usage policies and establish fairness checks for AI models. _(before Phase 4: Pilot Design)_

**4. R09 Security Vulnerabilities** — Security vulnerabilities pose a significant risk, especially with AI models that could be targeted by adversarial attacks.  
<sub>Threatens: “AI-powered tools into core business functions”</sub>  
Impact (register): Data breaches and operational risks  
Mitigation (register): Adopt AI security best practices and penetration testing  
Next step: Conduct a security review of the AI infrastructure and implement best practices to mitigate vulnerabilities. _(before Phase 5: Pilot Implementation)_

**5. R03 Talent & Skills Gap** — The project may face challenges due to a lack of internal AI expertise, which could slow down progress and increase reliance on external vendors.  
<sub>Threatens: “drive data-driven decision-making”</sub>  
Impact (register): Overreliance on external vendors and slow progress  
Mitigation (register): Provide staff training and hire specialized talent  
Next step: Initiate a staff training program focused on AI and machine learning skills to build internal capabilities. _(before Phase 4: Pilot Design)_

**6. R04 Change Resistance** — Resistance to change among employees could hinder the adoption of AI-driven workflows, impacting overall project ROI.  
<sub>Threatens: “improve customer experience”</sub>  
Impact (register): Low adoption and reduced ROI  
Mitigation (register): Strong change management and early engagement  
Next step: Implement a change management strategy that includes early engagement with employees to address concerns. _(before Phase 4: Pilot Design)_

**7. R06 Cost Overruns** — Cost overruns could jeopardize the project if AI development costs are underestimated, particularly as the project scales.  
<sub>Threatens: “lowering operational costs by 10%”</sub>  
Impact (register): Budget constraints and project delays  
Mitigation (register): Set realistic budget and build in contingency funds  
Next step: Review and adjust the project budget to include contingency funds for unforeseen costs. _(before Phase 5: Pilot Implementation)_

**8. R07 Unrealistic Expectations** — Unrealistic expectations from stakeholders regarding immediate ROI could lead to disillusionment and loss of support for the project.  
<sub>Threatens: “position ABCDE Ltd. as a technology-forward leader”</sub>  
Impact (register): Disillusionment and loss of support  
Mitigation (register): Align expectations and show quick wins  
Next step: Communicate a realistic timeline for ROI and highlight quick wins to maintain stakeholder support. _(before Phase 5: Pilot Implementation)_

**9. R08 Model Performance Drift** — Model performance drift is a long-term risk that could affect decision-making accuracy if not monitored regularly.  
<sub>Threatens: “uncover actionable insights from historical and real-time data”</sub>  
Impact (register): Incorrect decisions and trust erosion  
Mitigation (register): Regular retraining cycles and monitoring dashboards  
Next step: Establish a monitoring dashboard to track model performance and schedule regular retraining cycles. _(before Phase 6: Evaluation & Iteration)_

**10. R10 Vendor Lock-in** — Vendor lock-in could limit flexibility and increase costs in the future if the project becomes overly dependent on a specific AI platform.  
<sub>Threatens: “integrating AI-powered tools into core business functions”</sub>  
Impact (register): Flexibility loss and future switching costs  
Mitigation (register): Favor open standards and negotiate flexible vendor terms  
Next step: Negotiate flexible terms with vendors and consider open standards to avoid lock-in. _(before Phase 5: Pilot Implementation)_

---

Grounding check: 10/10 risks traced to the register and source ✅

Review checks (task-board consistency, actionable next steps): ✅
